items.headline: Haaland is the standout Gameweek 7 captain as City rotation clouds every other pick
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the clear captaincy choice for Gameweek 7 at home to Ipswich, with Manchester City expected to dominate despite possible rotation following Liverpool and PSG. Haaland is likely to start, though an early substitution is a realistic risk if City build a large lead. Ryan Cherki is the preferred City attacking punt if buying this week, as Ipswich should require creativity rather than defensive work, but Phil Foden’s return from suspension, Doku’s fitness and wider selection uncertainty make City midfielders short-term gambles rather than secure long-term investments. Start any City assets already owned, while Josko Gvardiol looks safer than O’Reilly in defence.

The recommended Triple Captain is Haaland against Ipswich for managers who still hold the chip. Ipswich have been especially vulnerable defensively and City have the attacking ceiling to exploit them, even with changes around Haaland. The downside is that Haaland has played heavy recent minutes and could be withdrawn early, while later home matches against Fulham and Hull offer alternative Triple Captain windows. Managers avoiding Haaland should look first to Joao Pedro, Kaoru Mitoma, Bukayo Saka or Cole Palmer, but none match Haaland’s combination of fixture and expected ownership.

Newcastle’s 4-1 defeat to Coventry raises concerns over Yoane Wissa, who is playing deeper and is not completely assured of his starting place as Newcastle seek more midfield control. Sell Wissa if there are three or more transfers available, although holding is acceptable if there are bigger problems elsewhere: Lewis Hall, Malick Thiaw and Harvey Barnes can be benched against Aston Villa before more attractive fixtures against Crystal Palace, Everton and Fulham. Joao Pedro is the priority replacement forward if absent; otherwise Calvert-Lewin ranks ahead of Aston Villa’s Jackson, Barry, Dominic Solanke and Evanilson. Calvert-Lewin offers price value and a useful longer-term fixture run, while Jackson is nailed, in form and benefits from Villa’s improving attack despite difficult upcoming matches against Newcastle and Manchester City.

Among budget midfielders, Aston Villa’s Manzambi is the preferred longer-term option over Tavernier, whose minutes have recently fallen after European matches and who may lose penalties when teammates return. Balumi, Coventry penalty-taker Rudoni and Hull regular Slater are cheaper alternatives, with Slater particularly useful for enabling a 3-4-3 structure. David Raya is the strongest goalkeeper buy as a secure route into Arsenal’s defence, while Calafiori is the leading Arsenal defender because of his left-back role and lack of European commitments. Morgan Rogers remains the best-value midfielder, Saka narrowly ranks above Palmer among premiums, and Pascal Gross is an immediate buy for any team that does not already own him.

Liverpool’s Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai are not ruled out, with Szoboszlai carrying the best chance of featuring at Brentford. Kevin Schade is already training after his shoulder injury and could return around Gameweek 8, so he is not an urgent sale, but should not be started if there is cover. Morgan Gibbs-White is doubtful for Nottingham Forest’s match against Arsenal, improving the appeal of Arsenal defensive assets and making him a bench candidate. Reece James is out for months after surgery, but that does not make Jordan Henderson a worthwhile buy.
key_points: Captain Haaland against Ipswich in Gameweek 7; he is also the preferred Triple Captain despite the risk of an early substitution.
Ryan Cherki is the best City attacking transfer punt, but Foden, Doku and rotation make City midfield buys risky beyond this week.
Sell Yoane Wissa ahead of Aston Villa if squad transfers allow, with Joao Pedro the first replacement priority and Calvert-Lewin the leading alternative.
Start owned Manchester City players unless reliable team news says otherwise; Gvardiol looks a safer defensive start than O’Reilly.
Manzambi is the preferred budget midfielder for the longer term, while Slater is a viable £4.5m enabler for a 3-4-3 squad.
Buy David Raya for a secure long-term Arsenal defensive slot and Calafiori as the standout Arsenal defender.
Szoboszlai has a better chance of playing than Isak or Gakpo, while Schade is training but is better benched until his return is confirmed.
Bench doubtful Gibbs-White against Arsenal; his possible absence boosts Arsenal clean-sheet prospects.

There is no planned transfer for Gameweek 7 after the Wildcard, with the intention to roll the next free transfer. The key decision remains the final defender slot, where Mhmovic is preferred to Hall because of Leeds’ home form and Newcastle’s recent lack of conviction.

items.headline: Haaland remains the Gameweek 7 captain despite Manchester City rotation talk
items.summary:
Erling Haaland remains the standout Gameweek 7 captain for Manchester City’s home match against Ipswich, despite comments that several heavily used players will need rests at some stage. The expectation is that any meaningful rotation is more likely to arrive in European or cup fixtures rather than a Premier League match City cannot afford to take lightly. Phil Foden returns from suspension and is backed to feature, while Cherki’s half-time withdrawal in midweek suggests he may also be preserved for the weekend. Managers considering Cherki need not be overly alarmed, although Foden’s return adds competition for attacking places.

Chelsea attackers receive a possible boost at Everton, where Jarrad Branthwaite is a late doubt with a dead leg and Everton’s defensive options remain stretched. Vitalii Mykolenko has a chance of returning, but Nathan Patterson is not ready to start. Chelsea have no fresh concerns among their main attacking options, although Reece James is out until at least Christmas after knee surgery. Brentford’s Kevin Schade is not ruled out after a shoulder issue and has trained on grass, but owners should have a reliable first substitute because his involvement is uncertain.

Liverpool’s key attacking injury doubts remain unresolved ahead of Brentford. Arne Slot leaves the door open for Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai to return, but provides no firm assurances, while Ryan Gravenberch is suspended. Newcastle’s Joelinton is closer to starting than Dan Burn, and Ross Barkley is a potential concern for Aston Villa after playing through pain in midweek; he is still relevant as a penalty taker if selected. Sunderland may regain Brian Brobbey and Habib Diarra, but Wilson Isidor is doubtful, potentially improving Brobbey’s route to minutes.

Defensive transfers are worth considering carefully. Arsenal’s Ben White is viewed as a risky pick because Jurrien Timber remains first choice at right-back and can reclaim the role at any time; moving White to a more secure starter such as Leeds’ Milos Kerkez is the suggested approach. Gabriel owners with two free transfers can consider switching to Bukayo Saka, whose midweek rest and attacking return strengthen his appeal, though Arsenal’s clean-sheet potential against Nottingham Forest remains high. Morgan Gibbs-White has a minor muscle issue but is expected to have a chance of playing, while Forest should welcome back Nikola Milenkovic to training.
key_points: Captain Erling Haaland for Manchester City’s home game against Ipswich, with rotation more likely in Europe or the cup than in Gameweek 7.
Phil Foden returns from suspension and is expected to be involved, while Cherki appears reasonably secure after limited midweek minutes.
Kevin Schade trains after his shoulder problem and is worth starting if owned, but use a strong first substitute.
Liverpool offer no firm fitness assurances on Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo or Dominik Szoboszlai, so their owners should monitor late news.
Chelsea attackers benefit if Everton are without Jarrad Branthwaite, while Reece James is sidelined until at least Christmas.
Avoid buying or consider selling Ben White due to Jurrien Timber competition; Bukayo Saka is the preferred Arsenal attacking pivot if funds and transfers allow.
Morgan Gibbs-White has a minor muscle injury but may still start for Nottingham Forest, while Nikola Milenkovic returns to training.
Wilson Isidor is doubtful for Sunderland, improving Brian Brobbey’s prospects after his return to the matchday squad.

items.headline: Haaland remains Gameweek 7 captain despite fresh rotation warning
items.summary:
Erling Haaland remains the leading captaincy pick for Manchester City’s home match against Ipswich in Gameweek 7, even after Enzo Maresca again says he needs rest. The expectation is that Haaland starts, with any rest more likely to arrive in the Champions League or Carabao Cup than in a Premier League fixture City should win. That said, the possibility of reduced minutes makes the Triple Captain call less certain; managers uncomfortable with the risk can wait for later options including Haaland at home to Hull in Gameweek 16, Bruno Fernandes at home to Coventry in Gameweek 14, or Bukayo Saka at home to Hull in Gameweek 10.

Morgan Gibbs-White is a doubt after failing to train with a minor muscle issue, but he is not ruled out for Nottingham Forest’s trip to Arsenal. He is worth holding, particularly with Ipswich away in Gameweek 8, and can still be started if there is credible bench cover; the likely outcomes are a start or no appearance, rather than a managed cameo. Brentford’s Sharda is also not fully fit and is safer to bench if possible, although his upcoming fixtures mean owners should generally hold. Brighton’s Mitoma is unlikely to become a serious selection concern before Gameweek 11, while the potential returns of Mint and Wea increase the longer-term rotation threat to Diper.

Diper is an excellent starter against Crystal Palace in Gameweek 7, but buying him now requires a plan for Liverpool away in Gameweek 8 and Manchester City away in Gameweek 9, when he is best benched. His place is not guaranteed once Brighton’s injured wide players return, so he is a luxury move only for squads with a strong bench, spare transfers and no immediate problems elsewhere. Arsenal defenders remain attractive: Califury benefits from Enapp’s continued absence, while Conza’s appeal could grow if Seliva’s next scan confirms a lengthy lay-off.

The main midfield warning is to avoid chasing Churkey at the expense of Saka. Churkey’s underlying numbers are outstanding and he is a viable buy for managers convinced he retains 70-to-80-minute starts, but Phil Foden’s return adds serious competition for the City number 10 role. Saka, by contrast, remains a hold despite two quiet gameweeks: he has three goals in six matches, strong minutes, likely penalties and a promising run of Forest away, Everton at home and Hull at home. For forward transfers, Calvert-Lewin is preferred to Whistler because of superior minutes, penalty security and Leeds’ stronger overall profile. Rather than dead-ending the third forward slot, it is currently more practical to dead-end a fifth midfielder, given the useful budget forwards available.

The proposed team move is Whistler to Calvert-Lewin, with Vardio to Van Hec a possible second transfer if there is evidence Vardio will not start against Ipswich. Vardio’s uncertain role creates a recurring headache, whereas Van Hec better suits a squad that does not need an extra defender in Gameweek 8 and values Palace at home in Gameweek 9. The preferred Gameweek 7 line-up uses a 4-3-3, starts Joao Pedro, benches Sosai because of his fitness flag, and keeps Haaland as captain rather than Triple Captain.
key_points: Captain Haaland against Ipswich in Gameweek 7, but delay the Triple Captain chip if Guardiola’s rotation comments make the risk uncomfortable.
Hold Morgan Gibbs-White despite his muscle-injury doubt; start him only with a reliable first substitute, as Ipswich away in Gameweek 8 is a strong fixture.
Bench Sharda if squad depth allows, but retain him for Brentford’s favourable fixture run if he returns quickly.
Buy Diper only if your squad can bench him for Liverpool away in Gameweek 8 and Manchester City away in Gameweek 9, while accepting future rotation risk from returning Brighton wingers.
Do not sell Saka to fund Churkey: Saka retains penalties, strong minutes and good Gameweeks 7-10 fixtures, while Churkey faces greater Foden-related rotation risk.
Calvert-Lewin is the preferred replacement for Whistler thanks to reliable starts and penalties; Whistler to Calvert-Lewin is the recommended transfer.
Choose Spurs defenders over Leeds defenders when Gameweek 7 and Gameweek 9 coverage matters, but Mahameraovic remains competitive for managers needing starts in the next two weeks.
Vardio is a sell-to-Van-Hec candidate if team news suggests he misses Ipswich, but can be kept for one more week if expected to start.

items.title: BEST SCHADE REPLACEMENTS ⚠️ | Josh's GW7 FPL Tips
items.headline: Pascal Groß tops Kevin Schade replacement list as Tavernier and Bailey offer upside
items.summary:
Kevin Schade’s injury forces Fantasy Premier League managers to look for a midfield replacement, with Brighton’s Pascal Groß presented as the preferred option for those who do not already own him. Groß is the standout all-round pick, while Newcastle’s Harvey Barnes is also flagged as a short-term alternative with Crystal Palace and Fulham among his next four opponents.

Aston Villa’s Leon Bailey is an attacking upside pick at £5.9m. Despite making only two Premier League starts, Bailey has one goal and two assists, making him an appealing option for managers willing to accept the risk around minutes in Villa’s competitive wide positions.

Bournemouth’s Marcus Tavernier offers a stronger combination of form, role and fixtures. He already has three league goals, Bournemouth are about to enter a favourable fixture run, and Tavernier is viewed as a central attacking figure for the side. That makes him a particularly attractive direct Schade replacement for managers targeting sustained returns rather than a one-week punt.

Hull City’s Jaden Philogene? No — Illiman Ndiaye is highlighted as the more unconventional selection, having produced three goals and two assists and ranking as the game’s fifth-highest-scoring midfielder. His recent stream of attacking and bonus-style returns makes him a differential consideration, although the pick carries more risk than established Premier League options. Groß remains the priority, with Tavernier the leading fixture-driven alternative and Bailey or Barnes offering higher-variance upside.
key_points: Pascal Groß is the number-one Kevin Schade replacement if he is not already in the squad.
Marcus Tavernier has three goals, a strong Bournemouth fixture run ahead and a key attacking role.
Leon Bailey costs £5.9m and has one goal and two assists from just two Premier League starts, but his minutes carry risk.
Illiman Ndiaye has three goals and two assists and is the fifth-highest-scoring midfielder, making him a differential option.
Harvey Barnes is a short-term consideration with Crystal Palace and Fulham in Newcastle’s next four fixtures.

items.title: FPL GW7 Expert Trends, Transfers & Best Captains 🧠 #fpl
items.headline: Haaland dominates Gameweek 7 captaincy as experts turn to Thiago and Cherki
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the overwhelming Gameweek 7 captaincy choice among the 100 FPL experts surveyed, with 97% backing the Manchester City forward. A small minority prefer Rayan Cherki or another Brighton option, but the captaincy market is far more settled than it was in Gameweek 6. Some managers even deploy the Triple Captain chip on Haaland, underlining the confidence in his ceiling this week.

Transfer activity focuses on attacking replacements. Thiago is the most popular incoming player after a 15-point haul, while Manchester City’s Rayan Cherki emerges as the favoured differential. Calvert-Lewin also gains support as a forward option, particularly for managers who already own João Pedro and need an alternative striker rather than doubling up on the same budget-forward route.

The main sales are Salah and Wissa, with around half of their expert owners moving them on. Lewis Hall and Martin Ødegaard also trend downwards. The moves reflect a willingness to sell underperforming or less secure assets to target recent attacking form, although buying Thiago after a major haul carries the usual risk of chasing points and Cherki remains a more speculative differential pick.

For Gameweek 7, the broad expert strategy is therefore straightforward: prioritise Haaland for captaincy, consider Thiago as the headline transfer target, and use Cherki or Calvert-Lewin to differentiate if squad structure and existing ownership make them suitable.
key_points: Erling Haaland is the captain for 97% of surveyed experts in Gameweek 7, with a few also using Triple Captain.
Rayan Cherki and Brighton players account for the small minority of non-Haaland captaincy selections.
Thiago is the most popular transfer in after his 15-point Gameweek 6 return.
Rayan Cherki is the leading differential target among expert managers.
Calvert-Lewin becomes a popular forward replacement, especially for managers who already own João Pedro.
Salah and Wissa are the most common transfers out, while Lewis Hall and Martin Ødegaard also lose support.

items.title: FPL GW7 EXPERTS TEAM 🚀 430x Top 10k! 🚨 BEST TEAM!
items.headline: Haaland dominates Gameweek 7 captaincy as Calvert-Lewin becomes the leading transfer target
items.summary:
Elite managers overwhelmingly captain Erling Haaland in Gameweek 7, with 99% backing the Manchester City forward and the only Haaland non-owner selecting Bukayo Saka. Haaland’s effective ownership is just under 200% among this group, meaning captaining him is primarily defensive rather than a route to major rank gains. Manchester City have the highest projected goal total of the week, while a sizeable 7% of managers deploy Triple Captain on Haaland.

The most popular transfer is Newcastle’s Joe Willock to Dominic Calvert-Lewin, with 20% selling Willock and 16% buying the Everton striker. Newcastle’s attack has disappointed despite a favourable run, while Willock faces competition for his role and is less appealing if used behind the centre-forward. Calvert-Lewin offers stronger long-term fixtures and 3.21 expected goal involvements so far. Budget-forward alternatives include Barry and Carvalho, while Gonzalo is viewed as a viable short-term hold but a less compelling new buy beyond his next two fixtures. João Pedro, Gross, Rogers and De Kyper are also among the main purchases.

Leeds defender Mahamutovic is highlighted as an unusually complete budget option. He combines clean-sheet potential with attacking threat and averages 11.33 defensive contributions per 90 minutes, enough to regularly earn the extra two DefCon points available to defenders who reach 10 in a match. His 67% DefCon hit rate is likely to fall, but he remains under 5% owned and is considered a strong differential. Managers are also weighing De Kyper against Van Hecke: De Kyper has been one of the season’s standout scorers, but Brighton’s tougher matches against Liverpool and Manchester City in Gameweeks 8 and 9 make Van Hecke a more pragmatic late entry for some.

Transfer strategy is generally cautious, with 47% rolling a free transfer for Gameweek 8 and 28% making one move. Wildcard squads favour a stable core of Raya, Haaland, Saka, Palmer, Gross, João Pedro and Calvert-Lewin, supplemented by DefCon defenders such as Silva, Calafiori, De Kyper, Mahamutovic and Thomas. One Bench Boost squad targets Gameweek 7’s broad fixture appeal before planning to bank transfers until Gameweek 11, while wildcard managers prioritise depth and defensive rotation rather than short-term punts. The consensus expert XI includes Kędźwierzynski, Castagne, Fofana, Konsa, De Kyper, Mitrović, Rodgers, Palmer, Gross, Haaland, Calvert-Lewin and João Pedro, with Gibbs-White, Hall and Mitrović close calls for starting places.
key_points: Captain Haaland in Gameweek 7: 99% of leading managers do so, while Saka is the sole alternative among Haaland non-owners.
Willock to Calvert-Lewin is the leading transfer, driven by Newcastle’s blunt attack and Calvert-Lewin’s superior fixtures and 3.21 xGI.
Mahamutovic is a low-owned Leeds defensive differential, averaging 11.33 DefCon per 90 and offering clean-sheet, attacking and bonus-point potential.
De Kyper remains a premium defensive target, but Van Hecke is preferred by some managers wary of Brighton’s Gameweek 8 and 9 matches against Liverpool and Manchester City.
Nearly half of elite managers roll a transfer this week, prioritising flexibility for Gameweek 8 rather than forcing moves.
Seven percent Triple Captain Haaland and 2% Bench Boost, while 3% use their Wildcard in Gameweek 7.
Raya is the preferred set-and-forget goalkeeper in wildcard drafts, while Calvert-Lewin, João Pedro and Haaland form the favoured forward line.

items.title: FPL GW7 Team Selection: Too Late to BUY De Cuyper? 🤔 | Transfers & Captain
items.headline: Haaland captaincy is locked as Hall-to-De Cuyper transfer tempts for Gameweek 7
items.summary:
A Gameweek 6 score of 67 causes a red arrow from 25,000 to 52,000, largely because Matty Cash's haul is missed and Bukayo Saka blanks as captain. However, the core squad is not judged to be in trouble. Guglielmo Kinsky remains a strong £4.5m goalkeeper pick for Coventry at home: Spurs rank second for expected goals conceded across the past five Gameweeks, behind Arsenal, and their fixture run is favourable apart from Chelsea in Gameweek 8.

The defence is led by Arsenal's Calafiori against Nottingham Forest, with Arsenal carrying a 42% clean-sheet probability and Calafiori offering attacking upside. Kolasinac also starts against Manchester United, a strong defensive-contribution fixture; he is already a leading DefCon defender, threatens from set pieces and faces an opposition that has produced defensive contributions for centre-backs. The decision between the safer clean-sheet route and a more explosive defender remains a consideration, while Lewis Hall is the weakest long-term member of the back line.

The midfield of Saka, Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Pascal Gross is retained. Saka's recent blanks are not enough to justify selling: he plays centrally alongside Kai Havertz, has penalties and some corners, and receives useful Champions League rest. Palmer, Rogers and Gross are all viewed as automatic holds. Dominik Szoboszlai is benched because he is doubtful after missing the midweek match and faces Brentford away, while Gross and Barry have attractive home fixtures against vulnerable defences. Szoboszlai is still not an urgent sale because he is a 90-minute player with penalties and set pieces, and Liverpool have Brighton at home in Gameweek 8 and Crystal Palace in Gameweek 10.

Erling Haaland is the clear captain against Ipswich, with the Triple Captain chip worth considering, while Gross is provisionally vice-captain. Joao Pedro remains essential, and Barry starts against Chelsea despite wasteful finishing because he leads the league alongside Haaland for shots in the box, Chelsea have conceded the third-most xG, and his volume gives him genuine multi-return potential. The likely transfer is Hall to De Cuyper, leaving three free transfers and £0.1m in the bank. Antonio Silva has appealing underlying numbers and defensive-contribution potential, but De Cuyper's 53 points versus Silva's 13, attacking role and immediate fixture appeal make the simpler, more form-led move attractive. European minutes and team news remain the final checks before confirming it.
key_points: Captain Haaland against Ipswich in Gameweek 7, with the Triple Captain chip a viable consideration; Gross is the tentative vice-captain.
Hold Kinsky for Coventry at home, as Spurs have the Premier League's second-best xG conceded record over the past five Gameweeks and a strong fixture run.
Start Calafiori against Nottingham Forest and Kolasinac against Manchester United, with the latter offering a particularly strong defensive-contribution profile.
Keep Saka despite his captaincy blank, as his central role, set pieces, penalties and managed Champions League minutes support a near-term return.
Bench the doubtful Szoboszlai against Brentford, but do not force a sale while Liverpool's Gameweek 8 and 10 fixtures remain playable.
Start Barry against Chelsea: he has elite shot volume, Chelsea's defence is conceding heavily, and his low price makes him easy to bench for tougher games such as Arsenal next week.
The preferred transfer is Lewis Hall to De Cuyper, although Silva remains an alternative with similar underlying attacking data and stronger defensive-contribution appeal.
Monitor European line-ups and minutes before finalising De Cuyper, especially for signs of injury, rotation or returning competition for his attacking role.

items.title: My Team Selection for Gameweek 7 #fpl #fantasypremierleague #fpltips
items.headline: Haaland wears the armband as Arsenal defensive triple-up anchors Gameweek 7
items.summary:
A 79-point Gameweek 6 return lifts the squad back inside the top 100,000, and the Gameweek 7 plan is built around a defensive bet on Arsenal. David Raya and Riccardo Calafiori start alongside Ezri Konsa, creating a three-man Arsenal defensive core in expectation of a clean sheet. Lewis Hall is the main alternative, with his greater attacking upside making the decision close, but Arsenal’s defensive reliability is preferred to Newcastle’s. Hall is therefore first substitute, providing useful cover.

Jamie Vardy is the principal selection risk after being benched against Liverpool. A home match against Ipswich is strong enough to justify taking the chance on his start, but another benching would likely prompt a sale, with Jan Paul van Hecke mentioned as the likely replacement. The midfield is settled: Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Pascal Groß are all considered strong options both this week and over the next run of fixtures.

Up front, Yoane Wissa is the transfer most likely to be made, with four free transfers available. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the preferred replacement, although Gonzalo García appeals for fixtures against Hull at home and Coventry away in the following week, while Thierno Barry offers a cheaper route. João Pedro is an easy hold, while Erling Haaland is the clear captaincy choice. Ibrahim Sangaré and Dominik Szoboszlai remain injury or availability concerns on the bench, but the strength of the starting side allows patience; Szoboszlai is retained partly because there is no obvious replacement and there is hope he returns for Gameweek 8 against Brighton at home.
key_points: Erling Haaland is the straightforward captain for Gameweek 7.
David Raya, Riccardo Calafiori and Ezri Konsa form a defensive triple-up based on confidence in an Arsenal clean sheet.
Lewis Hall loses out despite stronger attacking potential, but remains first substitute.
Jamie Vardy is started against Ipswich at home despite the risk of another benching after Liverpool.
Yoane Wissa is the likeliest transfer out, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin the preferred replacement.
Gonzalo García and cheaper Thierno Barry are alternative Wissa replacements, with García’s Hull and Coventry fixtures appealing.
João Pedro is held, while Sangaré and Szoboszlai are kept for another week because the squad has adequate cover and Szoboszlai may return in Gameweek 8.

items.title: "DO I NEED TO WILDCARD?" 🤔 | Nacho's GW7 Team Selection & Transfer Plans
items.headline: Verbruggen Gets the Nod Over a Tottenham Goalkeeper as Wildcard Wait Continues
items.summary:
With £0.6m in the bank and one free transfer available, the immediate decision is whether the squad finally needs a Wildcard. The answer remains no for now, although the pressure to use it is growing and the coming week is treated as a genuine reassessment point rather than an automatic hold.

The main selection call is in goal. Bart Verbruggen, at home to Crystal Palace, is preferred over the alternative goalkeeper option with Tottenham hosting Coventry. Verbruggen is considered the clear choice in this specific squad, principally because Brighton’s home fixture offers the stronger clean-sheet appeal. The calculation could be closer if there were already a Brighton defender in the starting XI, as doubling up on a defence increases the downside of conceding, but without that overlap Verbruggen is the straightforward play.

The defensive setup features Ezri Konsa, Timothy Castagne and Wesley Fofana, while Arsenal coverage is viewed as sensible. Kristoffer Ajer is also under consideration, driven by confidence in Brentford’s home form: Brentford are regarded as a strong defensive option at home against almost any opponent. However, there is an acknowledgement that this may be an optimistic reading of Ajer’s individual FPL potential, so he remains more of a fixture-based punt than a fully convincing long-term solution.
key_points: Hold the Wildcard for now, but reassess seriously this week rather than ruling it out again by default.
Start Bart Verbruggen at home to Crystal Palace ahead of the Tottenham goalkeeper option against Coventry.
Verbruggen’s selection becomes less clear if already doubling up on Brighton’s defence.
Konsa, Castagne and Fofana form the current defensive core, with double Arsenal coverage considered sensible.
Ajer is a possible defensive option because Brentford are trusted strongly in home fixtures, though his individual appeal carries risk.
The squad has one free transfer and £0.6m in the bank.

items.title: FPL GW7 WILDCARD TEMPALTE DRAFT! 🍟 CHERKI IN? 🧊 #fpl  #premierleague
items.headline: Haaland captains a Gameweek 7 Wildcard built around Arsenal defence and double Chelsea attack
items.summary:
The Gameweek 7 Wildcard draft is anchored by Erling Haaland as captain, with João Pedro vice-captain, and prioritises a premium Arsenal defensive double-up. David Raya starts in goal alongside Riccardo Calafiori, while William Saliba is viewed as too risky to bring straight back into the side. Ezri Konsa is another defensive option, but Ben Mee is selected to start because of a useful run of home fixtures, including Coventry, Ipswich and Crystal Palace over the next six matches.

Mee can be rotated with low-cost bench defenders Mepham of Leeds and Bobby Thomas, allowing the squad to target favourable fixtures without spending heavily at the back. The approach is to secure Arsenal clean-sheet potential through Raya and Calafiori, then use cheaper defenders with playable schedules rather than committing further funds to defence.

Midfield includes Morgan Rogers, Pascal Gross, Bukayo Saka and a punt on Ryan Cherki. Cherki offers upside but carries a minutes risk; Bournemouth's Marcus Tavernier is the safer downgrade if his role is not secure. Saka gets the nod over Cole Palmer because his underlying data is stronger, while the squad already carries two Chelsea attackers, making triple Arsenal feel like the more reliable structure. Slater is the budget bench midfielder, although Rodoni or Hull's Balogun are preferable at around £4.9m if team value permits.

Up front, Haaland and João Pedro are joined by Dominic Calvert-Lewin. Barry and Nicolas Jackson are considered alternatives, but Calvert-Lewin is preferred as the lead forward for a side trusted to perform well this season. The draft therefore balances premium captaincy security in Haaland with Arsenal defensive coverage, Chelsea attacking exposure and several lower-cost rotation options.
key_points: Captain Erling Haaland in Gameweek 7, with João Pedro as vice-captain.
Build the defence around David Raya and Riccardo Calafiori for an Arsenal double-up, while avoiding an immediate Saliba return.
Start Ben Mee for a favourable home run featuring Coventry, Ipswich and Crystal Palace, then rotate him with Mepham and Bobby Thomas.
Ryan Cherki is the midfield upside pick, but Marcus Tavernier is the fallback if Cherki's minutes look unsafe.
Bukayo Saka is preferred to Cole Palmer on underlying data, with double Chelsea attack already providing Blues exposure.
Dominic Calvert-Lewin is favoured as the third forward ahead of Barry or Nicolas Jackson.
Use Slater as the budget fifth midfielder, upgrading to Rodoni or Hull's Balogun if squad value allows.

items.title: My FPL GW7 TEAM SELECTION! 🔥 MAKING 2 TRANSFERS 🔒
items.headline: Haaland is the standout Gameweek 7 captain as Rogers becomes the priority transfer
items.summary:
Gameweek 6 brings a modest 61-point return, hurt by Saka’s captaincy blank and several non-returns, although Kyper’s 15 points continue an extraordinary start: two goals and three assists in six matches make him FPL’s top-scoring defender. João Pedro’s bench haul narrowly works out after King is brought in amid late concerns over Chelsea team news, but the episode reinforces a lesson not to overreact to volatile betting-odds movements.

For Gameweek 7, the defence looks strong enough to avoid spending a transfer. Van Hecke returns alongside Kyper, Konsa and Raya, giving exposure to sides with strong clean-sheet odds: Manchester City lead the way against Ipswich at 44%, followed by Arsenal against Forest at 42%, Tottenham at 38%, and Brighton and Fulham at 36%. Arsenal’s trip to Forest is not entirely comfortable, however, because Forest have produced more than 10 xG and 106 shots despite scoring only five goals.

The premium core of Haaland, Saka and Palmer looks settled. Haaland is the preferred captain at home to Ipswich after scoring twice against PSG in midweek, with City capable of a heavy win in what is framed as a revenge fixture. Saka remains a hold after recording elite underlying numbers and receiving a useful Champions League rest, while Gross is difficult to sell despite Brighton’s tougher Liverpool and Manchester City fixtures after Crystal Palace. Brighton lead the league for expected goals and face a Palace side bottom for expected goals conceded and shots conceded; managers with a strong bench can nevertheless consider sitting Kyper or Gross in the subsequent away matches.

The main concern is Whistler, whose Newcastle performances and underlying threat have not justified his place, particularly with doubts over his role behind Paro and possible competition for the No. 10 position. The favoured two-transfer move is Whistler to Barry and Szoboszlai to Rogers. Barry is cheap at £5.7m, likely has penalties, and ranks second only to Haaland for non-penalty xG after 13 big chances, even if his finishing remains unreliable. Rogers is the key target: he has returned in all but one game, regularly plays 90 minutes and looks like a long-term, potentially season-keeping Chelsea asset. The move also protects against imminent price rises, though it means benching Barry against Chelsea and committing to triple Chelsea attack alongside Palmer and João Pedro, which carries obvious downside whenever Chelsea fail to score.
key_points: Captain Haaland in Gameweek 7 against Ipswich; he is the clear top pick after a Champions League brace and City have the best clean-sheet odds as well.
Keep Saka, Palmer and Haaland as the preferred premium trio, with Bruno viewed as a sell after another blank and reports that he has carried an injury.
The preferred transfers are Whistler to Barry and Szoboszlai to Rogers, rather than rolling the transfer.
Rogers is the priority buy after returns in five of six gameweeks, regular 90-minute appearances and Chelsea’s high-scoring attack.
Barry costs £5.7m, is likely on penalties and ranks second in the league for non-penalty xG, but his missed chances make him a volatile pick.
Brighton assets Gross and Kyper are excellent for Crystal Palace, but their Liverpool and Manchester City away fixtures may justify benching them if squad depth allows.
Avoid making late decisions based heavily on betting-market shifts after the João Pedro benching call proves fortunate rather than sound.
Kyper remains a premium defensive hold after reaching two goals and three assists in six matches.

items.title: FPL EXPERTS! What You Need To Know 📊
items.headline: Experts tool adds live next-Gameweek teams, transfers and captaincy data from elite FPL managers
items.summary:
The Experts tool now shows the projected teams of leading all-time Fantasy Premier League managers for the upcoming Gameweek, with their transfers already factored in. This addresses the usual limitation of only being able to inspect teams from the previous round, giving users a view of what experienced managers are set to do before the deadline.

The data pool covers 273 highly ranked managers with a combined 430 top-10k finishes, including a former FPL champion. Users can see transfers in and out, providing a practical reference point when weighing up their own moves and identifying where elite-manager thinking is converging.

Captaincy choices for the next Gameweek are also displayed, alongside effective ownership figures. That helps managers assess the risk attached to backing a popular pick for protection or opposing the template in search of rank gains.

A full player-ownership list ranks selections from highest to lowest and compares expert ownership with overall FPL ownership. The gap between those figures can flag players strongly backed by elite managers but overlooked by the wider game. The feature is available through the FPL Focal app and fpl.page/experts, with membership advertised at 77p per week.
key_points: The tool shows elite managers' next-Gameweek squads rather than only their teams from the previous round.
Transfers in and out are included, offering a guide for managers deciding between competing moves before the deadline.
Next-Gameweek captaincy selections reveal where leading managers are concentrating their armband choices.
Effective ownership data helps assess whether to protect rank with a template pick or take a calculated differential risk.
Player ownership is compared between the expert group and the overall FPL population, highlighting potential under-the-radar targets.
The database covers 273 top managers with 430 combined top-10k finishes, including an FPL champion.

items.title: MY FPL GW7 TEAM SELECTION! 📱 Benching Decisions... 🪑 | Fantasy Premier League 2026/27
items.headline: Haaland remains captain as Harry rolls transfer after Gameweek 6 wildcard green arrow
items.summary:
A Gameweek 6 wildcard delivers 72 points and a rise from roughly 920,000 to 750,000 overall, with Toko-Ekambi’s 15 points at Sunderland the standout reward. Bryan Mbeumo also returns, while Bukayo Saka, Morgan Gibbs-White and Gonzalo García underwhelm despite encouraging underlying numbers. Saka creates more than Cole Palmer in a difficult match against Leeds, but Palmer’s appeal remains clear because Chelsea’s high-scoring attack gives him a greater route to returns. Gibbs-White is especially unlucky after being central to Nottingham Forest’s chances against Crystal Palace, while García misses two big opportunities.

The Gameweek 7 plan is to roll the sole free transfer and preserve flexibility after using too many early-season moves. David Raya stays in goal as a secure long-term Arsenal defensive route, while Riccardo Calafiori remains a priority starter after being rested in the Champions League, strengthening confidence that Arsenal manage him to start Premier League matches. Brighton defenders De Cuyper and Van Hecke are also set to start, with Van Hecke favoured at home to Coventry and De Cuyper retained for his advanced role despite a potential future minutes issue when Mitoma returns around Gameweek 11.

The main selection dilemma is Lewis Hall versus Mepham/Mahemo vich for the final defensive place. Newcastle’s four goals conceded to Coventry heighten concerns over Hall, while Aston Villa’s European scoring form makes a clean sheet less likely. However, Hall’s attacking threat keeps him narrowly ahead, whereas the alternative has a favourable home meeting with Manchester United and greater defensive-contribution potential. Gibbs-White is likely benched against Arsenal, partly because the squad already contains Raya and Calafiori, although his penalties and set pieces make him a viable alternative.

Morgan Rogers starts away to Everton, while Pascal Groß is backed against Crystal Palace, whose defensive data is poor and whose European commitments may further help Brighton. García also starts at home despite his recent misses: he is on penalties, continues to find chances and faces a Fulham side in need of points. Erling Haaland is the captain and João Pedro the vice-captain, with both regarded as the most reliable current FPL scorers and João Pedro preferred to Chelsea alternatives such as Palmer or Rogers. Longer term, García may be sold for Jackson if the latter’s form continues, while Hall or De Cuyper could become defensive transfer candidates.
key_points: Roll the Gameweek 7 free transfer to rebuild flexibility after the Gameweek 6 wildcard.
Captain Erling Haaland and vice-captain João Pedro, who are viewed as the two most dependable FPL attackers.
Start Raya, Calafiori, De Cuyper and Van Hecke, with Brighton’s home match against Crystal Palace a key fixture.
Lewis Hall is currently favoured over Mepham/Mahemo vich despite Newcastle’s poor display against Coventry, primarily because of his attacking upside.
Bench Morgan Gibbs-White against Arsenal despite his penalties and set pieces, as Raya and Calafiori already provide Arsenal defensive coverage.
Keep Gonzalo García for now because he is on penalties and getting big chances, but Jackson is a possible replacement in coming weeks.
Monitor De Cuyper’s minutes when Mitoma returns around Gameweek 11; Vuskovic is the likely defensive replacement route.

items.title: My FPL Team for GW7 🔥 Top 100k 🌍 Start/Bench/Sell Gvardiol 🤔
items.headline: Haaland captains Gameweek 7 as Gvardiol and Wissa face transfer pressure
items.summary:
A 79-point Gameweek 6, led by captain Cole Palmer's 16 points and another productive Brighton pairing of De Cuyper and Gross, lifts the rank from 131,000 to inside the top 75,000. The squad now has four free transfers and £1.1m in the bank, but the preference is to avoid spending them merely because they are available. Erling Haaland is the Gameweek 7 captain at home to Spurs, while Palmer, Morgan Rogers and João Pedro remain secure Chelsea attacking assets despite the risk that a triple-up occasionally produces multiple blanks.

The main immediate issue is Josko Gvardiol. He starts in Europe but remains at risk of rotation with O'Reilly for Manchester City’s home match against Ipswich. The upside is substantial if he starts, given his attacking threat, so he is currently selected; however, reliable news that he is benched could trigger a move to Brighton’s Van Hecke, with Bournemouth’s Silva another option. Both offer regular starts and an appealing run of home fixtures, whereas Gvardiol threatens to become a recurring selection headache. Konsa is preferred to Lewis Hall this week, largely because Arsenal’s clean-sheet potential is stronger than Newcastle’s, although Hall remains a capable first substitute.

Wissa is the other likely sale. He is no longer consistently playing as Newcastle’s central forward, chances are falling to Fernandez-Pardo, and Asprilla’s return increases the risk to his minutes. Wissa to Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the most probable transfer, with Leeds’ fixture run offering attractive home matches even if difficult away trips limit the ceiling. Calvert-Lewin is preferred to shorter-term alternatives such as Barry or Gonzalo Garcia because he looks the more durable squad option. De Cuyper stays despite Liverpool and Manchester City fixtures in Gameweeks 8 and 9: at £4.5m, he is playing high on Brighton’s left and can simply be benched for those tougher games.

Szoboszlai and Sangaré are retained for now despite their problems. Szoboszlai is flagged but could return for Brighton at home in Gameweek 8, while there is no compelling £6m-£6.5m midfield replacement to force an early move. Sangaré cannot secure a Brentford start, but can remain a bench player, with a possible opening if Janelt receives a fifth yellow card. The longer-term ambition is to use accumulated transfers around Gameweek 9 to fund Bukayo Saka, potentially by downgrading Konsa, Sangaré and Gvardiol. Saka is attractive as a differential captain for Arsenal’s Gameweek 10 home match against Hull, especially with penalty duties and strong expected minutes.
key_points: Erling Haaland is the Gameweek 7 captain at home to Spurs, with João Pedro and Palmer also locked into the squad.
Wissa to Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the likeliest transfer because Wissa’s role and minutes are deteriorating while Leeds have useful upcoming home fixtures.
Gvardiol starts for now against Ipswich, but a credible benching leak could prompt a move to Van Hecke; Silva is the secondary defensive target.
Konsa is favoured over Lewis Hall because Arsenal offer the better clean-sheet outlook, though Hall is a viable first substitute.
De Cuyper is retained at £4.5m while he continues to play on Brighton’s left wing, with plans to bench him in Gameweeks 8 and 9 if needed.
Szoboszlai and Sangaré are likely benched rather than sold, preserving transfers until there is a clearer midfield target or injury update.
Saka is a Gameweek 9-10 target, with Arsenal’s Gameweek 10 home fixture against Hull presenting a potential differential captaincy opportunity.
A possible Free Hit in Gameweek 12 and future switches to Manchester United assets for Gameweek 14 are being considered, but rolling transfers remains the priority.
